test_title: SSC CGL Tier 2 Quant Previous Year Paper (Held On: 3 Feb 2022)
subject: general
question: The ratio of the investments of A and B in a business is 7 ∶ 5, and the ratio of their profits at the end of a year is 2 ∶ 5. If A invested the money for 6 months, then for how much time (in months) has B invested his money?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time Ratio = (Profit Ratio ÷ Investment Ratio)

TA : TB = (2 ÷ 7) : (5 ÷ 5) = 2/7 : 1 = 2 : 7

Since 2 units of time = 6 months, then 1 unit = 3 months.

B’s time = 7 units = 7 × 3 = 21 months.

**∴ The correct answer is 21 months.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Investment Ratio (A : B) = 7 : 5

Profit Ratio (A : B) = 2 : 5

Time for A (TA) = 6 months

**Formula Used:**

Profit = Investment × Time

ProfitA ÷ ProfitB = (InvestmentA × TimeA) ÷ (InvestmentB × TimeB)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ea0df21f69f4524434c32e8189f926c6fc4831c5127fb3b5a1d51c5bb07864b9.png] 

Let the time for which B invested his money be TB.

⇒ 2 ÷ 5 = (7 × 6) ÷ (5 × TB)

⇒ 2 ÷ 5 = 42 ÷ (5 × TB)

⇒ 2 × 5 × TB = 42 × 5

⇒ 10 × TB = 210

⇒ TB = 210 ÷ 10

⇒ TB = 21 months

**∴ The correct answer is 21 months.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Partnership Profit Ratio

When multiple partners invest, the profit is distributed in the ratio of the product of their capital and time period: P₁ : P₂ = C₁ × T₁ : C₂ × T₂.

Types of Partners

An active partner manages the business and may take a salary before profit sharing, while a sleeping partner only contributes capital.

Ratio of Time and Capital

Time ratio (T₁ : T₂) = (P₁/C₁) : (P₂/C₂) and Capital ratio (C₁ : C₂) = (P₁/T₁) : (P₂/T₂).</p
